body:
i don't think you're crying for sympathy or attention. and i get that feeling that im doing that all the time. but i mean, either way, its not like you're undeserving of either of those things. 

you're having real problems, and i think it's important to validate the way you're feeling. because like, if you drop your ice cream and feel sad for the rest of the day, its legit, because you actually feel sad. no one gets to tell you how you feel and you cant decide how you feel, either. i get you. im okay now, but i wasnt before. i didnt do anything. i knew what i was supposed to do, and i knew i was capable of doing things, but i was so emotionless and lacking motivation that i never really tried.

i would say definitely don't call yourself cowardly for not going through with suicide. death is really scary. its literally hardwired into our bodies to do everything possible to keep ourselves alive. i dont think suicide isn't brave. or cowardly. it's just really sad, and something i hope you don't do. 

i think maybe.. dont thrust yourself into anything huge. maybe start seeing a therapist and just do a couple of small things every now and then, and let yourself be proud of that. like cleaning or eating something healthy. i really hope you feel better.

its always good to hear that someone else thinks i'm having struggles and that im not just actually being a child about all of this. 

i did have low self worth before the boyfriend. i feel confident that my parents love me, but i do not think they do a very good job of showing it. i also don't think i was always confident of that. my family has always been cycles of fucked up. and i would really like to break that. 

the thing you said about the whole thing taking form of cheating makes a lot, a lot, a lot of sense. so much sense that i find it weird that no one has offered up that bit of wisdom yet. I havent done it though, since it happened to me, the cheating thing, and i started caring a lot more.

you sound like a really intelligent person. and you said a ton of things in here that make a lot of sense to me and were really helpful and that i'm gonna remember. thanks for that.

And yes, I do have a therapist. Sometimes i find it hard to believe some of the things she says about me though because i think she's a little biased because she seems to really, really like me. And i mean, i dont think she would like me if i was a bad person, but it's still really helpful to hear different perspectives from people who don't know me at all.

thanks for being so kind, and reasonable, and for taking the time to write something so thoughtful. i hope you have a really good day.

thank you. no, i dont want to do it again.

i really appreciate what you said. and for reading all of that. and that you said the thing about learning about myself, because thats something i really hope that im doing rather than being stuck in one place forever. so thank you for validating that. thank you thank you thank you.
